publisher: U.S. Department of Commerce, Bureau of Industry and Security
source_title: Commerce Implements New Export Controls on Advanced Computing and Semiconductor Manufacturing Items to the People’s Republic of China (PRC)
claim_relevant_visible_text: Adds new license requirements for items destined to a semiconductor fabrication “facility” in the PRC that fabricates ICs meeting specified thresholds. The relevant memory thresholds are DRAM memory chips of 18nm half-pitch or less and NAND flash memory chips with 128 layers or more.
researcher_paraphrase: BIS's October 2022 rule made advanced PRC memory-fab equipment access conditional on licensing at explicit DRAM and NAND technology thresholds.
precision_guard: This is a regulatory threshold and licensing rule, not evidence that any particular fab was denied equipment, stopped production, lost wafers or reduced bit output.
authority_boundary: BIS is authoritative for the U.S. export-control rule and stated thresholds.
